card.title: Derivatives: Inverse Trigonometric, Exponential and Logarithmic

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic derivatives come from one engine — (f⁻¹)′ = 1/f′ — plus branch discipline and the Pythagorean dictionary; every singularity of an inverse derivative is the original's horizontal tangent made visible. The exponential family orbits e: the self-replicating base pays no ln a tax, every other base wears one, and the log's reciprocal rule completes the inverse pair.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Omitting the minus sign on the arccos derivative — it is the one inverse trig derivative that is negative among the three principal ones.  ·  Writing $\frac{d}{dx}a^x = a^x$ instead of $a^x\ln a$; only the natural exponential is self-derivative.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Omitting the minus sign on the arccos derivative — it is the one inverse trig derivative that is negative among the three principal ones.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The branch decides the sign*** - on y in [-pi/2, pi/2], cos y >= 0 forces the positive root in (sin^-1)' - the ± temptation dies at the branch.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Dropping the absolute value in the arcsec and arccsc derivatives.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Derive, do not recall: state the engine, name the branch, read the sign.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Derive (tan⁻¹x)′ = 1/(1 + x²) using the inverse-engine rule, stating the branch.** — **Setup:** y = tan⁻¹x ⟹ x = tan y with y ∈ (−π/2, π/2) — the principal branch, on which tan is one-to-one and sec y > 0. **Engine:** (tan⁻¹)′(x) = 1/(tan)′(y) = 1/sec²y.…  ·  **NEB-style (5m): Differentiate y = 5ˣ and y = log₃x, making each base tax explicit.** — **Exponential:** (5ˣ)′ = 5ˣ·ln 5 — the general-base tax ln 5 ≈ 1.609; only e pays none. **Logarithm:** (log₃x)′ = 1/(x·ln 3) — the same tax in the denominator; equivalently log₃x = ln x/ln 3 and the constant multiple rule delivers it.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State domains with inverse trig derivatives - |x| < 1 or |x| > 1 is part of the answer.

rows.label: Classified table
rows.text: Derivative families for inverse, exponential and log — classified · Family | Derivative | Domain note · arcsin / arccos | 1/sqrt(1-x^2) and its negative | Only on (-1, 1) · arctan / arccot | 1/(1+x^2) and its negative | All real x · exp | (e^x)' = e^x | Fixed point of differentiation · General exponential | (a^x)' = a^x ln a | ln a factor is the exam trap · Logarithm | (ln x)' = 1/x | x > 0 only; (log_a x)' = 1/(x ln a)

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One engine and branch discipline replace six memorisations; e is the unique base whose derivative is itself.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Inverse-engine rule: (f^-1)'(f(x)) = 1/f'(x), f' != 0 - derives the whole inverse trig table. Entries: sin^-1 -> 1/sqrt(1-x^2); tan^-1 -> 1/(1+x^2); sec^-1 -> 1/(|x|sqrt(x^2-1)); co-functions carry minus signs; branches supply positivity.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The ln a factor is the general-base tax; e is the unique base that pays none.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (5m): Differentiate y = sin⁻¹(3x) and state the domain of the answer.** — **Chain rule (outer table, inner derivative):** (sin⁻¹)′(u) = 1/√(1 − u²) with u = 3x, u′ = 3 ⟹ y′ = 3/√(1 − 9x²).…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Using the inverse-engine rule, derive (sec⁻¹x)′ = 1/(|x|√(x² − 1)) and explain the absolute value.** — **Setup:** y = sec⁻¹x ⟹ x = sec y, y ∈ [0, π] \\ {π/2} (the principal branch). **Engine:** (sec⁻¹)′(x) = 1/(sec)′(y) = 1/(sec y·tan y) = 1/(x·tan y).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to Inverse Trig, Exp and Log Derivatives This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to derivatives of inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions: the inverse-engine rule and the base-e story in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Inverse-engine rule:** if f is invertible and differentiable with f′ ≠ 0, then (f⁻¹)′(f(x)) = 1/f′(x) — differentiate the identity f⁻¹(f(x)) = x by the chain rule. - **Inverse trig table:** (sin⁻¹x)′ = 1/√(1−x²); (cos⁻¹x)′ = −1/√(1−x²); (tan⁻¹x)′ = 1/(1+x²); (cot⁻¹x)′ = −1/(1+x²); (sec⁻¹x)′ = 1/(|x|√(x²−1)); (cosec⁻¹x)′ = −1/(|x|√(x²−1)).…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — One Engine, Six Derivatives - The inverse-engine rule derives the **entire inverse trig table**: sin⁻¹ via 1/cos y = 1/√(1−x²) (the positive root forced by the principal branch); tan⁻¹ via 1/sec²y = cos²y = 1/(1+x²). One theorem plus branch discipline replaces six memorisations.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Differentiate y = 5ˣ and y = log₃x.  ·  Differentiate y = sin⁻¹(3x).  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Branches Supply the Signs - The inverse trig derivatives' signs come from the **principal branches**: on y ∈ [−π/2, π/2], cos y ≥ 0, so the square root in (sin⁻¹)′ is positive; the co-function minus signs are the branch's mirror. Sign errors in this table are almost always branch errors.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — engine derivation:** derive one inverse trig entry from the rule, stating the branch. - **Type B — base conversions:** (aˣ)′ and (log_a x)′ with the ln a tax made explicit. - **Type C — chain-wrapped entries:** sin⁻¹(u), ln(u), eᵘ with the inner derivative attached.…  ·  ## 6.
